title: BOHA! goes printer-agnostic
summary: BOHA! food labeling software is now in beta on select Zebra label printers. See who qualifies, how it fits with BOHA! hardware, and how to apply.
body_markdown:
## Your Software Shouldn’t Wait on Your Printers


Every foodservice operator knows the moment. You’ve found a back-of-house platform that could tighten food safety, speed up productivity and give leadership real visibility and control across locations. Then comes the catch: before you can roll it out, you need to replace the printers already sitting in your kitchens.


For many operators, that’s where good intentions stall. The hardware still works. The budget cycle isn’t there yet. And so the software that could make a difference today gets pushed to next year.


We don’t think it should work that way. That’s why we’re advancing a printer-agnostic strategy for the[BOHA! SaaS Platform](https://www.transact-tech.com/software/boha-saas-platform) , starting with a beta program that invites operators to test BOHA! software on the Zebra label printers they already own.


## Software First, on Your Timeline


The value of a back-of-house platform lives in the software: the workflows, the standards, the data. Hardware should support that value, not gate it.


By working toward support for eligible Zebra printers, we’re removing one of the most practical barriers to adoption. Operators shouldn’t have to wait for existing printers to reach the end of their useful life before they can start running a better kitchen.


As our CEO John Dillon put it, the goal is to bring BOHA! to more kitchens “regardless of where those operators are in their hardware investment cycle.” That’s a meaningful shift. It means the decision to adopt BOHA! can be made on the merits of the platform, not on the age of the equipment in the back room.


## More Than a Label: One Connected Platform


Here’s what sets BOHA! apart: it was never just about printing labels. BOHA! is a unified SaaS platform that brings together the applications a modern kitchen depends on, including[labeling](https://www.transact-tech.com/solutions/food-prep-labeling) ,[temperature monitoring](https://www.transact-tech.com/software/boha-temp) ,[checklists](https://www.transact-tech.com/software/boha-checklist) ,[timers](https://www.transact-tech.com/software/boha-timer) ,[HACCP reports](https://www.transact-tech.com/resources/blog/how-to-build-a-haccp-plan-for-a-restaurant) and training.


Those tools don’t live in silos, and weren't cobbled together from different vendors. They were purpose-built to remove chaos in the kitchen, while connected through one BOHA! Control Center, giving enterprises centralized management and visibility across every location. A district manager can see whether checklists are getting done. A food safety lead can track temperature logs. An operations executive can push a menu change across hundreds of stores and know it landed consistently, and see brand standards being met.


That breadth is exactly why a printer-agnostic approach matters. When the software is this central to how a kitchen runs, the faster operators can get it into every location, the faster they see the return. Opening the door to existing hardware lets the full platform reach more kitchens sooner.


## Why BOHA! Hardware Is Still the Best Way to Run BOHA!


Opening the platform to more printers doesn’t change our view of what the best experience looks like.[BOHA! Terminal 2, BOHA! WorkStation and Ithaca 9000](https://www.transact-tech.com/hardware/label-printers) remain our flagship, purpose-built solutions, and they’re designed to get the most out of the BOHA! platform.


The biggest difference is the dual print mechanism. With two print mechanisms built into one device, a kitchen can run two label types side by side without swapping media, so prep labels and grab-and-go labels, for example, are both ready the moment a team member needs them. Fewer roll changes means less downtime during a rush and fewer chances for the wrong label to end up on the wrong product.


BOHA! hardware also supports a wide range of label sizes, from small day-dot and prep labels to larger formats for[grab-and-go packaging](https://www.transact-tech.com/resources/blog/fresh-food-labeling-systems-scale) , nutrition information and allergen details. That range lets one device handle the full spectrum of what a kitchen prints, instead of spreading the work across multiple machines.


Add in the[integrated software experience](https://www.transact-tech.com/resources/blog/boha-terminal-2-wireless-printing) , where hardware and platform are engineered together, and you get a solution that’s faster to deploy, simpler to manage and built specifically for the realities of a commercial kitchen. Broader printer support is a starting point; BOHA! hardware is where operators can go as their replacement needs arise and their operations grow.


## A Rollout Strategy That Fits Your Business


The printer-agnostic direction is about giving operators more control, and it opens two clear paths.


For existing BOHA! customers, planned Zebra support would let you extend BOHA! software into locations that already have eligible Zebra printers, before those locations purchase BOHA! hardware. That means one standard platform across your whole footprint, sooner, rather than a patchwork of systems while you wait on equipment refreshes.


For new customers, it creates an entry point to BOHA! using equipment you already own. You can experience the platform’s workflows, centralized control and enterprise visibility without an upfront hardware investment, then move to purpose-built BOHA! hardware on a schedule that makes sense.


In Dillon’s words, customers can “standardize on BOHA! software while modernizing their printers on a schedule that works for their business.” It’s a model built around the operator’s timeline, not the vendor’s.


## Join the Beta


This is just the first step, and we want operators to help shape it. We’re looking for existing and prospective customers in restaurants, contract foodservice and convenience stores who use Zebra label printers and want to evaluate BOHA! in their operations.


Beta participants will help us validate printing performance, workflow fit and deployment requirements, and their feedback will inform potential commercial availability. It’s a chance to see BOHA! running in your own kitchens, on your own equipment, and to have a direct voice in where the program goes next.


To apply, email:BETA@TransAct-tech.com and share your Zebra printer models, connectivity setup, number of locations and the labeling workflows you have in mind. Participation is subject to technical qualification, and the beta will evaluate select Zebra models, configurations and workflows; it does not represent general availability or support for all Zebra printers.


The back-of-house platform your kitchens need shouldn’t have to wait on a hardware cycle. With this beta, it doesn’t have to.
